headline: Sherrill vetoes two Jersey City revenue bills amid budget crisis
dek: New Jersey's governor rejected a proposed car-rental tax and a measure allowing temporary diversion of open-space funds as the city confronts a projected $250 million shortfall.
body: Gov. Mikie Sherrill vetoed two bills Monday that were written to give Jersey City additional ways to raise or redirect money as the city confronts a projected budget shortfall of about $250 million.

One bill, S-4514, would have created a 5% tax on motor-vehicle rentals in Jersey City and changed how certain municipal vehicle-related taxes, fees and penalties could be used. The governor's veto statement says the city is the only municipality that meets the bill's population and growth thresholds.

The second bill, S-4513, would have allowed Jersey City to temporarily move money from a voter-approved levy for open space, recreation and historic preservation into its general fund during fiscal year 2027. Sherrill wrote that the levy was approved for those purposes and that the bill would set aside the condition under which voters accepted the added tax.

Jersey City's own financial report describes the projected gap as roughly 28% of the city's operating budget. The report says projected 2026 expenses exceed $922 million while revenue is expected to be about $667 million, though the city is continuing to close its prior-year books and refine the figures.

The New Jersey Monitor reported that the bills were intended to help the city close the gap and that the vetoes were Sherrill's first since taking office. The governor's action leaves city officials facing the shortfall through budget reductions, structural changes and other revenue decisions rather than the two measures she rejected.
author: NorthEast News Desk
